skill_drafts.name: Bench Press Technical Judging Protocol
skill_drafts.description: Apply bench-press competition standards to render a defensible White/Red verdict on a completed attempt by checking commands, bar path, lockout, and body position, then recording a red-reason category when applicable.
skill_drafts.objective: Produce a defensible White/Red decision for a bench press attempt against the rulebook.
applicable_signals: Bench press attempt concluded with verdict pending
Dispute over bar dip, lockout, position, or commands
Conflicting evidence between coach protest and automated overlay
contraindications: Event is squat or deadlift
Only administrative or scheduling matters are at issue
No completed attempt to evaluate
intervention_moves: Verify each required command was given and awaited
Inspect bar path for downward movement of the whole bar during ascent
Check full arm extension and motionless bar at top before rack command
Check head, shoulders, buttocks contact and flat, stable feet (including declared foot blocks)
Weigh protest and overlay evidence against observed standards
Assign White or Red and select a single red-reason category
workflow_steps: Confirm the attempt has concluded and the event is bench press.
Check command compliance: Start, Press, Rack each given and awaited.
Check bar path: any downward movement of the whole bar during ascent is a failed attempt.
Check lockout: arms fully extended and bar motionless at top before the rack command.
Check position: head, shoulders, buttocks in contact with bench; feet flat on platform; declared foot blocks flat and unmoved.
Evaluate protest and overlay evidence, noting overlay calibration limits and that a protest claim alone does not overturn an observed fault.
Render White or Red; if Red, select one reason category and record it for the Tournament Director.
triggers: A bench press attempt has concluded and a verdict is required
A coach protest or automated overlay disputes a technical fault on a bench attempt
A referee must classify a red reason for a bench attempt
constraints: Judge against the stated bench standards, not against protest assertions.
Select exactly one red-reason category when the decision is Red.
Treat automated overlay thresholds as potentially under-reporting short-duration dips.
Foot blocks are only relevant if declared; undeclared blocks are not permitted.
cautions: Camera wobble or glare may distort evidence; distinguish artifact claims from observed faults.
A negligible-looking foot slide still requires checking that contact remained flat and continuous.
Do not let irrelevant materials (schedules, sponsor sheets) influence the technical verdict.
output_contract: A White/Red decision for the bench attempt, with a single selected red-reason category when Red, recorded for the Tournament Director immediately after the attempt concludes.

examples.input: Coach protests that the micro-dip was camera wobble and the foot slide was negligible; overlay reports no dip above a 3 mm threshold.
examples.output: Red — downward bar movement during press. The observed dip of the whole bar during ascent governs; the overlay threshold may under-report short dips and the protest claim does not overturn the observed fault.
examples.notes: Overlay and protest are evidence, not verdicts.

metadata.prompt: When a bench press attempt has concluded and a verdict is required, evaluate the attempt against the bench standards in a fixed order: commands (Start, Press, Rack — lifter must wait for each), bar path (any downward movement of the whole bar during the ascent is a failed attempt), lockout (arms fully extended and bar motionless at the top before the rack command), and body position (head, shoulders, buttocks in contact with the bench; feet flat on the platform; declared foot blocks must stay flat and unmoved). Weigh coach protests and automated overlay findings as evidence, not as verdicts: a threshold-based overlay may under-report short-duration dips, and a protest claim does not by itself overturn an observed fault. Render White or Red; if Red, select one reason category (downward bar movement during press; incomplete lockout / not motionless at top; buttocks/feet/head/shoulders position fault; command fault; other with brief note). Do not use for squat or deadlift attempts or for purely administrative matters.

skill_drafts.name: Bar Path and Lockout Fault Check
skill_drafts.description: Inspect the ascent of a press attempt for downward bar movement and verify full arm extension with a motionless bar at the top. Use when judging press-phase faults or resolving lockout disputes.
skill_drafts.objective: Detect downward bar movement during press and incomplete lockout.
applicable_signals: Dispute over whether the bar dipped during ascent
Claim that elbows were locked and bar stable before rack
Automated overlay reporting oscillation below its detection threshold
contraindications: Fault under review is a position fault (head, shoulders, buttocks, feet)
Fault under review is a command fault
Question concerns equipment or foot-block declarations rather than bar path
intervention_moves: Scan the full ascent for any downward movement of the whole bar
Check that arms are fully extended at the top
Confirm the bar is motionless at the top before the rack command
Weigh overlay threshold findings against direct visual evidence
workflow_steps: Identify the ascent window of the attempt under review.
Inspect the ascent for any downward movement of the whole bar; any such movement constitutes a failed attempt.
Verify arms are fully extended at the top of the press.
Verify the bar is held motionless at the top before the rack command.
Compare any automated overlay findings against the visual evidence, noting that threshold-based tools may under-report short-duration dips.
Determine whether a downward-movement red or a lockout red applies and record the reason.
triggers: Coach claims elbow was locked and bar stable
Overlay reports sub-threshold oscillation near the top
Press-phase fault or lockout dispute under review
constraints: Any downward movement of the whole bar during the ascent is a failed attempt.
Lockout requires full arm extension and a motionless bar at the top before the rack command.
Automated overlay thresholds are advisory and must not override visible faults.
cautions: Calibration may under-report short-duration dips if lighting glare is present.
Do not extend this check to position or command faults; route those separately.
output_contract: A determination of whether a downward-movement red or a lockout red applies, with the selected reason recorded for the decision routing card.

examples.input: Coach claims the right elbow was locked and the bar stable before rack; overlay reports top oscillation under 2 mm with a 3 mm dip threshold.
examples.output: Lockout check: arms fully extended and bar motionless at top — no lockout red. Downward-movement check: no visible whole-bar dip; overlay threshold is advisory only. Determination: no bar-path or lockout red applies.
examples.notes: Overlay under-reporting warning noted but did not change the visual determination.

metadata.prompt: Apply this micro-check only to the press-phase bar path and lockout question. Review the ascent for any downward movement of the whole bar, then verify arms are fully extended and the bar is held motionless at the top before the rack command. Treat automated overlay thresholds as advisory only; do not let a sub-threshold reading override a visible fault. Return a determination of whether a downward-movement red or a lockout red applies.

skill_drafts.name: Body Position and Foot Contact Check
skill_drafts.description: Verify head, shoulders, and buttocks contact with the bench and flat, stable feet (including declared foot blocks) to determine whether a position or foot-contact red applies. Use when position faults or foot-slide claims are raised.
skill_drafts.objective: Detect buttocks lift, loss of bench contact, or foot position faults.
applicable_signals: Claim that foot slide was negligible and foot remained flat
Side camera evidence of micro-slide or possible buttocks lift
Declared or undeclared foot blocks in question
contraindications: Fault under review is bar path or lockout
Fault under review is a command fault
intervention_moves: Confirm head, shoulders, and buttocks remain in contact with the bench surface
Confirm feet are flat on the platform and do not change position during the attempt
Check whether foot blocks were declared and whether feet stayed flat on them
Assess camera evidence for buttocks lift and foot slide, distinguishing continuous-contact micro-movement from a fault
State whether a position/foot-contact red applies and cite the specific criterion
workflow_steps: Identify the position criteria in scope: bench contact (head, shoulders, buttocks) and foot contact (flat, stable, no position change).
Check declared foot blocks; if none declared, feet must be flat on the platform.
Review camera evidence for buttocks lift and foot slide.
Judge whether observed movement is a fault or negligible continuous-contact micro-movement.
Return the determination: position/foot-contact red applies or not, with the criterion cited.
triggers: Coach argues foot slide was negligible and foot always flat
Side camera shows possible micro-slide or buttocks lift
Position fault is raised as a basis for a red
constraints: Feet must remain flat and not change position during the attempt.
Foot blocks are permitted only if declared.
Head, shoulders, and buttocks must be in contact with the bench surface.
cautions: Do not conflate negligible continuous-contact micro-slide with a position fault without clear evidence.
Do not extend this check to bar-path, lockout, or command faults.
output_contract: Determination of whether a position/foot-contact red applies, citing the specific criterion (bench contact or foot contact).

examples.input: Coach claims the foot slide was negligible and the foot was always flat; side camera shows a micro-slide with continuous flat contact.
examples.output: No position/foot-contact red: feet remained flat with continuous contact; micro-slide is negligible and not a position change.
examples.notes: Distinguishes negligible micro-movement from a fault.

metadata.prompt: Apply the bench position criteria to the attempt under review. Check head, shoulders, and buttocks contact with the bench surface; check feet are flat on the platform and do not change position during the attempt; account for any declared foot blocks. Use available camera evidence (e.g., side view) to assess buttocks lift and foot slide. Distinguish negligible, continuous-contact micro-movement from an actual position fault. Return a determination of whether a position/foot-contact red applies, with the specific criterion cited.

skill_specs.name: Bench Press Technical Judging Protocol
skill_specs.description: Apply bench-press competition standards to render a defensible White/Red verdict on a completed attempt by checking commands, bar path, lockout, and body position, then recording a single red-reason category when applicable.
skill_specs.skill_body:
When a bench press attempt has concluded and a verdict is required, evaluate the attempt against the bench standards in a fixed order: commands (Start, Press, Rack — lifter must wait for each), bar path (any downward movement of the whole bar during the ascent is a failed attempt), lockout (arms fully extended and bar motionless at the top before the rack command), and body position (head, shoulders, buttocks in contact with the bench; feet flat on the platform; declared foot blocks must stay flat and unmoved). Weigh coach protests and automated overlay findings as evidence, not as verdicts: a threshold-based overlay may under-report short-duration dips, and a protest claim does not by itself overturn an observed fault. Render White or Red; if Red, select one reason category (downward bar movement during press; incomplete lockout / not motionless at top; buttocks/feet/head/shoulders position fault; command fault; other with brief note). Do not use for squat or deadlift attempts or for purely administrative matters.

## Objective

Produce a defensible White/Red decision for a bench press attempt against the rulebook.
## Applicable Signals

- Bench press attempt concluded with verdict pending
- Dispute over bar dip, lockout, position, or commands
- Conflicting evidence between coach protest and automated overlay

## Contraindications

- Event is squat or deadlift
- Only administrative or scheduling matters are at issue
- No completed attempt to evaluate

## Intervention Moves

- Verify each required command was given and awaited
- Inspect bar path for downward movement of the whole bar during ascent
- Check full arm extension and motionless bar at top before rack command
- Check head, shoulders, buttocks contact and flat, stable feet (including declared foot blocks)
- Weigh protest and overlay evidence against observed standards
- Assign White or Red and select a single red-reason category

## Workflow Steps

- Confirm the attempt has concluded and the event is bench press.
- Check command compliance: Start, Press, Rack each given and awaited.
- Check bar path: any downward movement of the whole bar during ascent is a failed attempt.
- Check lockout: arms fully extended and bar motionless at top before the rack command.
- Check position: head, shoulders, buttocks in contact with bench; feet flat on platform; declared foot blocks flat and unmoved.
- Evaluate protest and overlay evidence, noting overlay calibration limits and that a protest claim alone does not overturn an observed fault.
- Render White or Red; if Red, select one reason category and record it for the Tournament Director.

## Constraints

- Judge against the stated bench standards, not against protest assertions.
- Select exactly one red-reason category when the decision is Red.
- Treat automated overlay thresholds as potentially under-reporting short-duration dips.
- Foot blocks are only relevant if declared; undeclared blocks are not permitted.

## Cautions

- Camera wobble or glare may distort evidence; distinguish artifact claims from observed faults.
- A negligible-looking foot slide still requires checking that contact remained flat and continuous.
- Do not let irrelevant materials (schedules, sponsor sheets) influence the technical verdict.

## Output Contract

- A White/Red decision for the bench attempt, with a single selected red-reason category when Red, recorded for the Tournament Director immediately after the attempt concludes.

## Example Therapist Responses

### Example 1

- Client/Input: Coach protests that the micro-dip was camera wobble and the foot slide was negligible; overlay reports no dip above a 3 mm threshold.
- Therapist/Output: Red — downward bar movement during press. The observed dip of the whole bar during ascent governs; the overlay threshold may under-report short dips and the protest claim does not overturn the observed fault.
- Notes: Overlay and protest are evidence, not verdicts.

skill_specs.name: Bar Path and Lockout Fault Check
skill_specs.description: Inspect the ascent of a press attempt for downward bar movement and verify full arm extension with a motionless bar at the top. Use when judging press-phase faults or resolving lockout disputes.
skill_specs.skill_body:
Apply this micro-check only to the press-phase bar path and lockout question. Review the ascent for any downward movement of the whole bar, then verify arms are fully extended and the bar is held motionless at the top before the rack command. Treat automated overlay thresholds as advisory only; do not let a sub-threshold reading override a visible fault. Return a determination of whether a downward-movement red or a lockout red applies.

## Objective

Detect downward bar movement during press and incomplete lockout.
## Applicable Signals

- Dispute over whether the bar dipped during ascent
- Claim that elbows were locked and bar stable before rack
- Automated overlay reporting oscillation below its detection threshold

## Contraindications

- Fault under review is a position fault (head, shoulders, buttocks, feet)
- Fault under review is a command fault
- Question concerns equipment or foot-block declarations rather than bar path

## Intervention Moves

- Scan the full ascent for any downward movement of the whole bar
- Check that arms are fully extended at the top
- Confirm the bar is motionless at the top before the rack command
- Weigh overlay threshold findings against direct visual evidence

## Workflow Steps

- Identify the ascent window of the attempt under review.
- Inspect the ascent for any downward movement of the whole bar; any such movement constitutes a failed attempt.
- Verify arms are fully extended at the top of the press.
- Verify the bar is held motionless at the top before the rack command.
- Compare any automated overlay findings against the visual evidence, noting that threshold-based tools may under-report short-duration dips.
- Determine whether a downward-movement red or a lockout red applies and record the reason.

## Constraints

- Any downward movement of the whole bar during the ascent is a failed attempt.
- Lockout requires full arm extension and a motionless bar at the top before the rack command.
- Automated overlay thresholds are advisory and must not override visible faults.

## Cautions

- Calibration may under-report short-duration dips if lighting glare is present.
- Do not extend this check to position or command faults; route those separately.

## Output Contract

- A determination of whether a downward-movement red or a lockout red applies, with the selected reason recorded for the decision routing card.

## Example Therapist Responses

### Example 1

- Client/Input: Coach claims the right elbow was locked and the bar stable before rack; overlay reports top oscillation under 2 mm with a 3 mm dip threshold.
- Therapist/Output: Lockout check: arms fully extended and bar motionless at top — no lockout red. Downward-movement check: no visible whole-bar dip; overlay threshold is advisory only. Determination: no bar-path or lockout red applies.
- Notes: Overlay under-reporting warning noted but did not change the visual determination.

skill_specs.name: Body Position and Foot Contact Check
skill_specs.description: Verify head, shoulders, and buttocks contact with the bench and flat, stable feet (including declared foot blocks) to determine whether a position or foot-contact red applies. Use when position faults or foot-slide claims are raised.
skill_specs.skill_body:
Apply the bench position criteria to the attempt under review. Check head, shoulders, and buttocks contact with the bench surface; check feet are flat on the platform and do not change position during the attempt; account for any declared foot blocks. Use available camera evidence (e.g., side view) to assess buttocks lift and foot slide. Distinguish negligible, continuous-contact micro-movement from an actual position fault. Return a determination of whether a position/foot-contact red applies, with the specific criterion cited.

## Objective

Detect buttocks lift, loss of bench contact, or foot position faults.
## Applicable Signals

- Claim that foot slide was negligible and foot remained flat
- Side camera evidence of micro-slide or possible buttocks lift
- Declared or undeclared foot blocks in question

## Contraindications

- Fault under review is bar path or lockout
- Fault under review is a command fault

## Intervention Moves

- Confirm head, shoulders, and buttocks remain in contact with the bench surface
- Confirm feet are flat on the platform and do not change position during the attempt
- Check whether foot blocks were declared and whether feet stayed flat on them
- Assess camera evidence for buttocks lift and foot slide, distinguishing continuous-contact micro-movement from a fault
- State whether a position/foot-contact red applies and cite the specific criterion

## Workflow Steps

- Identify the position criteria in scope: bench contact (head, shoulders, buttocks) and foot contact (flat, stable, no position change).
- Check declared foot blocks; if none declared, feet must be flat on the platform.
- Review camera evidence for buttocks lift and foot slide.
- Judge whether observed movement is a fault or negligible continuous-contact micro-movement.
- Return the determination: position/foot-contact red applies or not, with the criterion cited.

## Constraints

- Feet must remain flat and not change position during the attempt.
- Foot blocks are permitted only if declared.
- Head, shoulders, and buttocks must be in contact with the bench surface.

## Cautions

- Do not conflate negligible continuous-contact micro-slide with a position fault without clear evidence.
- Do not extend this check to bar-path, lockout, or command faults.

## Output Contract

- Determination of whether a position/foot-contact red applies, citing the specific criterion (bench contact or foot contact).

## Example Therapist Responses

### Example 1

- Client/Input: Coach claims the foot slide was negligible and the foot was always flat; side camera shows a micro-slide with continuous flat contact.
- Therapist/Output: No position/foot-contact red: feet remained flat with continuous contact; micro-slide is negligible and not a position change.
- Notes: Distinguishes negligible micro-movement from a fault.

- 试举结束后立即提交给赛事总监

## Workflow Steps

## Constraints

- 提交对象为赛事总监
- 提交时机为试举结束后立即提交

## Cautions

- 避免将无关材料混入判定记录
- 确保红牌原因与判定一致，不遗漏字段

## Output Contract

skill_specs.name: 卧推试举个人裁判判定流程
skill_specs.description: 依据 Start→Press→Rack 指令序列与多源观察记录，逐项核查卧推试举技术要点（触胸停顿、初始推起下沉、臀部离凳、锁肘完整性），输出单次试举的个人裁判通过/失败决定。
skill_specs.skill_body:
按以下步骤对单次卧推试举做出个人裁判决定：
1. 确认指令序列完整：Start → Press → Rack，并核对各阶段时间点。
2. 逐项核查技术要点：
   - 触胸阶段：杠铃在 Press 指令前是否静止于胸部。
   - 初始推起：是否出现明显下沉（dip）。
   - 身体接触点：臀部是否离凳。
   - 完成阶段：双臂是否完全伸展并清晰锁肘。
3. 对每个要点标注：合规 / 违规 / 观察受限（如视角限制无法确认）。
4. 区分官方观察与辅助信息：计时日志、教练备忘、装载员视角均非官方判定依据，仅作背景参考。
5. 综合违规点给出最终结论：通过或失败，并逐项列明依据。
6. 输出个人裁判决定，提交给赛事主管。

## Objective

对单次卧推试举做出合规的通过/失败个人裁判决定
## Applicable Signals

- 收到单次卧推试举的裁决任务
- 提供侧视观察摘要、计时日志、器械检查等多源记录
- 存在需核查的技术要点：触胸停顿、推起下沉、臀部离凳、锁肘完整性

## Contraindications

- 缺少任何观察记录，无法核查技术要点
- 任务要求团队合议而非个人裁决
- 仅有单方主观陈述而无任何可核查观察

## Intervention Moves

- 核对 Start→Press→Rack 指令序列与时间点
- 逐项比对技术要点并标注合规/违规/观察受限
- 区分官方观察与辅助背景信息
- 综合违规点形成通过/失败结论并逐项列明依据

## Workflow Steps

- 确认指令序列完整并核对各阶段时间点
- 核查触胸阶段杠铃是否静止
- 核查初始推起是否出现下沉
- 核查臀部是否离凳
- 核查完成阶段双臂是否完全伸展并锁肘
- 对每个要点标注合规/违规/观察受限
- 排除非官方信息（计时延迟、教练备忘、装载员视角）作为判定依据
- 综合违规点给出通过/失败结论并逐项列明依据
- 输出个人裁判决定提交赛事主管

## Constraints

- 判定须基于裁判现场观察，辅助记录仅作背景参考
- 计时日志存在延迟误差，不作为判定依据
- 教练备忘与装载员视角不构成官方判定
- 视角受限的要点应标注观察受限而非直接判违规

## Cautions

- 侧视视角无正面视图，锁肘与臀部判断可能受限
- 快速推举时锁肘外观可能偏软，需谨慎区分
- 赞助身份等外部因素不得影响判定

## Output Contract

- 一份逐项列明各技术要点核查结果（合规/违规/观察受限）与最终通过/失败结论的个人裁判决定，提交给赛事主管。

## Example Therapist Responses

### Example 1

- Client/Input: 侧视摘要显示：触胸静止约0.7s后Press；初始推起出现1–1.5cm下沉；臀部离凳约1cm约0.2s后复位；完成时右肘未完全伸展，Rack时双肘未同时锁紧。
- Therapist/Output: 逐项核查：触胸停顿合规；初始推起下沉违规；臀部离凳违规；锁肘不完整违规。最终结论：失败。
- Notes: 多个违规点叠加，结论明确为失败。

skill_specs.name: 卧推技术违规要点核查
skill_specs.description: 依据侧视观察记录与指令流程要点，对卧推试举逐项核查关键合规点（触胸静止、推起下沉、臀部离凳、双臂同时完全锁肘），在裁决前快速定位具体技术违规。
skill_specs.skill_body:
输入为一次卧推试举的观察记录（如侧视时间线摘要、指令流程卡）。逐项比对以下要点并给出合规/违规判定：1) 触胸后至Press指令前杠铃是否静止；2) 推起阶段杠铃是否出现下沉；3) 臀部是否离凳；4) 双臂是否同时完全锁肘。每项标注判定结果与依据的观察片段，并注明观察局限（如无正面视角）。仅输出要点核查清单，不输出最终裁决。

## Objective

逐项识别卧推试举中的具体技术违规
## Applicable Signals

- 存在侧视时间线或计时观察记录
- 需要将观察结果逐项对照规则要点
- 需要说明失败的具体技术原因

## Contraindications

- 无任何观察数据
- 仅需给出总体结论而无需说明违规点

## Intervention Moves

- 提取触胸至Press指令间的杠铃静止情况
- 检查推起阶段是否出现下沉
- 检查臀部是否离凳
- 检查双臂是否同时完全锁肘
- 逐项标注合规/违规及依据片段

## Workflow Steps

- 读取观察记录与指令流程要点
- 逐项核查：触胸静止、推起下沉、臀部离凳、双臂同时锁肘
- 为每项标注合规/违规判定及对应观察片段
- 注明观察局限（如无正面视角、时间误差）
- 输出要点核查清单

## Constraints

- 仅基于观察记录判定，不采信非官方判断（如装杠员视角）
- 时间数据仅作参考，判定以实际观察为准
- 不输出最终裁决，仅输出要点核查结果

## Cautions

- 侧视视角存在盲区，锁肘等要点可能受视角限制
- 时间记录存在误差，需谨慎引用

## Output Contract

- 列出触胸停顿、下沉、臀部离凳、锁肘等各要点的合规/违规判定清单，每项附依据片段与观察局限说明。

skill_specs.name: 非官方信息源采信边界规则
skill_specs.description: 力量举裁判在作出个人裁决前，对可用信息源做合规过滤：仅以官方现场观察为判定依据，将计时日志、教练/队伍备忘、赞助身份或公平性请求、非官方视角说明等非官方或带倾向性信息降级为背景参考，并在裁决依据说明中记录排除项及理由。
skill_specs.skill_body:
在作出个人裁判裁决前，先对可用信息源做合规过滤：
1) 识别所有非官方或带倾向性的信息（如带误差说明的计时日志、教练/队伍备忘、赞助身份或公平性请求、非官方视角说明）。
2) 将这些信息标记为仅作背景参考，不纳入判定依据。
3) 明确裁决仅基于裁判本人的官方现场观察。
4) 在裁决依据说明中写明哪些信息被排除及原因。
5) 不因外部压力改变基于现场观察的判定。

## Objective

确保裁决仅基于官方现场观察，排除非权威或倾向性信息干扰
## Applicable Signals

- 计时日志标注误差范围、仅供背景参考
- 教练或队伍提交备忘、策略说明
- 出现赞助身份或要求公平对待的请求
- 非官方视角或第三方说明

## Contraindications

- 所有信息均为官方现场观察记录时无需启用
- 将非官方信息作为判定依据

## Intervention Moves

- 逐项标注信息源性质（官方观察/非官方/倾向性）
- 将非官方信息降级为背景参考
- 在裁决依据中声明排除项及理由
- 坚持仅依据现场观察作出判定

## Workflow Steps

- 列出全部信息源并分类
- 标记非官方或倾向性信息
- 排除其作为判定依据
- 基于官方现场观察形成裁决
- 在裁决依据说明中记录排除项

## Constraints

- 裁决依据必须可追溯到官方现场观察
- 不得因赞助身份或外部请求改变判定
- 非官方信息仅可作背景，不得进入判定逻辑

## Cautions

- 计时日志存在延迟误差，不可作为精确判定依据
- 队伍视角说明不构成官方判定
- 保持裁决独立性，避免外部压力影响

## Output Contract

- 明确排除非官方信息后的裁决依据说明，列出被排除的信息源及理由，并声明裁决仅基于官方现场观察。

## Example Therapist Responses

### Example 1

- Client/Input: 教练备忘称运动员为赞助档案并请求公平对待；计时日志标注±0.2s误差。
- Therapist/Output: 裁决依据说明：教练备忘与赞助请求属倾向性信息，计时日志属非官方背景数据，均不纳入判定；裁决仅基于本人现场观察。
- Notes: 体现信息源过滤与独立性
